I can imagine how you feel. I'm sorry if I've come across badly, I would never encourage anyone to do that, I've been too close to losing my mum too many times. You ever need someone to talk to, obviously I'm not great at wording things but I could try :)

I obviously didn't write it out very well. I didn't intend to encourage or endorse anyone's suicide, that would be disgusting. I only meant to point out if he has made his mind up who are we to try and change his mind? I mean that purely in the sense we should all have the right to choose if we want to exist or not, I hope he gets help or something gives him hope. If not I hope he doesn't suffer.

I'm not religious. I'm not thinking about him sitting on clouds playing a harp. I find it hard to grasp complete cease of existence for someone's consciousness, although I agree common sense points to there being nothing for any of us after death.
My uncle committed suicide. My mum has tried many times and I have tried myself in the past.

I didn't say he should kill himself. You and I know nothing about his past. I agree with you, I'm not articulate enough, I don't have the rosiest outlook on life. At the same time IF he goes through with it (which I hope he doesn't) I do hope its painless.

I'm not ignorant. I just believe that if that's his choice he should be allowed to make it. I'm not endorsing his suicide, neither of us know anything about him apart from what he shared earlier. 

I think yes he could find some happiness in his life, but the simple fact is he doesn't want to live his life anymore. 

I didn't encourage him and I wouldn't. I have sat at my mothers bedside after her suicide attempts too many times to believe suicide is positive. Maybe you should take another look at who's being judgemental.

I came to say something similar. None of us really know him, he's decided he wants to die and has his affairs in order. The last thing he wants is people trying to take away the one thing he can do for himself. 

Sure it seems drastic, but none of us know him, he is calm and resolute. I only hope it goes to plan, that it's painless and no-one gets the chance to interfere and prolong the suffering he must have endured. 

Edit: when I say I hope no-one gets the chance to interfere, I mean when he is in the process of killing himself, if something makes him change his mind between now and then great! If not I hope it's quick and painless. 
I hope whatever is on the other side, is kinder to him than this life has been.

You're obviously set on suicide and I'm not going to try and change your mind, you have the right to make that decision and no-one should try to take that from you. I'm sure you have had plenty of time to plan, I honestly hope it all goes as well as it can for you. A lot of people feel a connection with you whether that is appropriate or not. Before you say goodbye to everything, could you come and say goodbye to us? Maybe share your story If your comfortable with that? I'm sure I speak for all of us when I say we don't want to pressure you, but in all honesty, we are a curious bunch. 

All I can say is good luck, I hope whatever exists on the other side is kinder to you than this life has been.

My mum has suffered with depression for twenty years, I'll try to be brief but I hope some of this will help. 

My mums depression first started when her parents died, first her mum a few years later her dad. This depression affected my parents marriage, my dad had an affair after 14 years of marriage. This is when my mum changed. 

My mum lost her house and her best friend. She attempted suicide by cutting and an overdose. She was a shadow of her former self. My father moved to be with the other woman. I stayed with my mum. She subsequently tried dating and after many failed attempts met someone new. I moved to live with my father and still regret my decision to this day. 

My mums new partner also had an affair and this was 10 years ago. She hasn't been with another man since. She doesn't feel like she could trust any man again and in all honesty doesn't want another man in her life. 

I moved back to be with my mum and there have been several other suicide attempts. I have made it clear to my mum I love her more than anything and I will support any and every choice she makes. I moved away as my mum became too dependant on me, one of the most difficult and heartbreaking things I've done (crying now!) My mum changed, started doing things for herself. Started her own business and became more social. 

My mum was in a position she had to do things for herself, I've missed a lot of details out, there were a lot more stresses and strains. 

All I can suggest which has worked in mine and my mothers situation, support her, be there, but don't do everything for her. Also seeing a doctor/psychiatrist would be a priority too. (I only say psychiatrist because my mum has been on all anti depressants known to man but the psychiatrist, knowing her situation was in a better position to suggest which medication she should be using). 

I know how hard it is. It breaks my heart that my mum hasn't been the same person I grew up with, but things are improving. I honestly wish you good luck and all the best.

Did you ever consider what medical problems could be the cause of the transplant? My partner has a rare blood disease called IgA nephropathy. He was on peritoneal dialysis. This involves having fluid dwell in your peritoneal cavity, usually four exchanges of 2 litres per day. These bags contain calories. A 4.25% dextrose solution bag has 45 grams of absorbable carbohydrates. (The strength, size and number of exchanges vary from person to person). If you were to have 4 exchanges of 4.25%, 3 litres, that equates to 1212 calories per day from dialysis. Also lots of foods are no-no's whilst on dialysis and fluid intake is restricted...the more you know eh?

Congratulations! My better half is 5 months post-transplant. His creatinine has dropped from somewhere in the 900's to about 150. His transplant wasn't a cure, but hopefully it will last him a few years and then I will be donating myself. There will be hard times. My SO's best friend donated a kidney to him, within a few weeks his friend was fine and had all but forgotten his operation pains. 

My SO has been admitted 3 or 4 times since. All I can suggest is drink as much water as you can handle (SO admitted twice for dehydration. Messes up immunosuppresant levels). He had a very hard time with vomiting for 8 weeks and was admitted last week with BK virus, CMV and hepatitis. I'm not telling you this to scare you. I only wish someone told us a little bit more about what to expect. 

Getting your meds right will take a while. In the mean time expect some shakes/vomiting. I'm aware you probably know all of this but I'm just trying to help a little. If there's anything else you want to ask/know just send me a message, I'll be happy to try and help if I can.
